summary.title: Language-agnosticism #40: delegate __init__.py literals to package_init_name()
summary.what: scope/carve._carve_module now names a package-init module after its directory only when path.name == grammar.package_init_name() (was: path.stem != '__init__'). graph/build._module_names_for_path takes an init_name parameter and gates the parent-package import spellings on `init_name is not None and fp.name == init_name` (was: fp.name == '__init__.py'); the caller passes m._grammar.package_init_name(). Added test_package_init_delegation.py. Suite 210->212.
summary.why: The package-init filename was hardcoded as a Python literal in shared carve/graph code -- the same overfit class as #34/#36/#37/#39. A non-Python file named like an init file would wrongly get package-init naming and import spellings. package_init_name() already existed as the per-grammar fact (Python '__init__.py', None elsewhere); these were the two remaining consumers still using the literal.
summary.user_goal: Language-agnosticism #40: delegate the hardcoded __init__.py literals in scope/carve.py + graph/build.py to grammar.package_init_name()

decisions.point: Whether new tests were needed given existing coverage
decisions.chose: Added one focused unit test on the delegation gate; relied on existing martin-zones/corpus-measures tests for the end-to-end Python path
decisions.rationale: test_rule_martin_zones already exercises Python __init__.py package import resolution (import core.thing -> the core package) and corpus_measures/runts cover init-trivial detection. The one gap was the agnostic half -- that a None init_name skips the branch -- so test_package_init_delegation pins exactly that plus package_init_name being Python-only.
rejected: Re-asserting the end-to-end Python path (redundant with martin-zones)
No new test (leaves the non-Python gating unpinned)

decisions.point: Scope of the sweep -- are there other __init__ literals in shared code?
decisions.chose: Swept the active redesign tree; fixed only carve + graph
decisions.rationale: The remaining __init__ literals in redesign live inside the Python grammar itself (python.py resolve_packages + package_init_name) -- those ARE the per-language fact and are correctly Python-specific. runts.py is Python-by-construction (parses Python line syntax, only runs on init modules). No other shared-code literal remains.

rejected.alternative: Also reworking resolve_packages (#5) in this pass
rejected.reason: Reframed as a fidelity enhancement, not a de-overfit bug (dep graph resolves edges by module name, not package; resolve_packages already has a neutral default + isolated Python override). Sequenced separately per the user's call.
